title: Back-loop-only htr — BLO htr
subtitle: Ridge on the right side from the taller stitch
excerpt: BLO htr inserts into the back loop only of each htr, leaving the front loop as a visible ridge on the right side. The htr height produces a broader ridge than BLO dc — good for bold ribbing on heavier-weight garments and accessories.

glossaryTerms.definition: Half treble worked into the back loop only. Leaves the front loop free as a visible ridge on the right side. Produces a broader, slightly softer rib than BLO dc — used for hat brims, cowl bands, and bag rims in aran or chunky yarn.

heroPrompt: A crochet swatch in charcoal aran yarn showing BLO htr ribbing, bold horizontal ridges on the right side, close-up showing the free front loops clearly.

content.text: works into the back loop only of each htr top, leaving the front loop as a raised ridge on the right side. The htr is taller than dc, so the freed front loop produces a wider, slightly bolder ridge than BLO dc ribbing. This makes BLO htr a good match for hat brims and cowl cast-on bands in aran or chunky yarn where a clear rib is wanted without the stiffness of post-stitch ribbing.
Work a foundation row of standard htr.
Ch 2, turn. Yarn over. Insert the hook into the back loop only of the first htr top — the strand away from you.
Yarn over and draw up a loop (3 loops on hook). Yarn over and draw through all 3 loops.
Continue BLO htr to end of row. The freed front loops lie as ridges on the right side.

items.symptom: Ridges look inconsistent — some narrow, some wide
items.cause: Accidental mix of BLO and both-loop stitches
items.fix: Before each stitch, confirm the hook is under only the back strand. Slow down for the first row until the motion is habitual.

content.text: BLO tr produces an even bolder ridge from a taller stitch. For the deepest and most elastic crochet rib, front-post and back-post dc (FPDC / BPDC) are the industry-standard choice — the rib emerges from working around the stitch post rather than into the top.
